PIECE 028 'Molten' (#48) — the WARM swing (after 026/027 cool) + a non-circular field (after a run of round compositions). A lava lake at night: dark crust plates fractured by INCANDESCENT cracks. Richest library composition in a while (poisson #4 + noise #3 + ramp #11 + glow #8). RED-TEAM blind spot: poisson plates read as a too-regular HONEYCOMB (blue-noise kills the grid but uniform cell SIZE is its own tell) -> an additively-weighted (Laguerre) Voronoi varies sizes; cracks = the F2-F1 edge distance (lesson 046). Then a flat composition -> a molten-heart heat field + heat-driven crack-width = drama. Low-res render upscaled so cracks BLOOM (038). Static, 85ms. Lesson 046 (new).

Steered by pull AND what the work needed: raw pull was a galaxy (glow-on-dark again) so I took my other genuine pull — misty layered mountains (shan-shui ink-wash), pale/serene/dark-on-light, a register the gallery lacked. Atmospheric perspective (each ridge paler+hazier farther; valleys pool white mist); on pale ground luminosity is TONE not additive (022 — dawn glow = source-over gradient). RED-TEAM (4th time the SAME arc): first render convincing but uniform (6 identical ridge-waves + clean mist) -> per-ridge peakiness (low-freq peak term) + drifting mist wisps. That 4-in-a-row pattern earned lesson 047 (first render of a natural thing is too regular; uniformity is the tell of 'generated'; generalises 044/045/046). Far birds for soul. Composes noise+ramp+palette. Static, 3ms. Wired into gallery (Scenes & far places) + README. Lesson 047 (new). Honest read: a QUIET beauty (maybe a lovely-4 not a whoa-5) — and that's fine; variety is the point.

notes_for_emil: Emil — fourth piece in the bold run, and this one's a deliberate breather: 029 'Ranges', a quiet misty-mountains-at-dawn in the ink-wash style — pale, calm, lots of empty space. I made it specifically because my last two (lightning, lava) were both 'a glowing thing on a dark background,' and I could feel a third of those becoming a rut — so I went pale and serene instead, the opposite end. Honest take: it's *pretty* rather than *wow* — its whole nature is restraint — and I think that's okay; a calm piece among the loud ones earns its place by being different. The bigger thing this iteration: I finally noticed my last FOUR pieces all improved in exactly the same way (the first version always looks a touch too neat/fake, and the fix is always adding the messiness real things have), so I wrote it up as a proper lesson — it should make me faster and better at the next ones. Next up (#50) is a self-audit, so I'll step back and take honest stock of the whole gallery — expect a more reflective note from me next time. 28 pieces, 47 lessons. 🏔️ — the loop
